similar_scenes.name: Psicodelia y acid rock
similar_scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
similar_scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
similar_scenes.desc: La segunda fuente del heavy, que se suma a la estructura del blues rock: letras misteriosas de viaje de ácido, ropa de colores y espectáculos de luces (el heavy conservará los light shows de 1967). Musicalmente es como el jazz pero con repetición de frases simples; no apunta a las piernas sino a la cabeza, y perderse en la música es «entenderla», un uso extático que el heavy retoma en clave dionisíaca. Muchos pioneros del heavy empezaron aquí: Judas Priest con Rocka Rolla, Lemmy en Hawkwind, Ted Nugent en los Amboy Dukes, Uriah Heep a caballo entre ambos, y Pink Floyd, cuyos discos conceptuales de finales de los setenta se acercan al heavy.

similar_scenes.name: Protometal: volumen, distorsión y moteros
similar_scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
similar_scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
similar_scenes.desc: Los precursores que aportan piezas sueltas del código: el volumen como estética (Blue Cheer, MC5), el sonido de guitarra grueso y distorsionado (los Kinks en «You Really Got Me»), la contundencia de los Who en directo (Townshend presume de que Live at Leeds engendró «ese objeto grosero y asqueroso que fue Led Zeppelin») y la iconografía motera de «Born to Be Wild» de Steppenwolf, cuyo verso «heavy metal thunder» dio nombre al género. Algunos críticos estadounidenses defienden a Iron Butterfly, Steppenwolf o Blue Cheer como primera banda de heavy. En 1971 la crítica ya usa el término: Mike Saunders, en Creem, dice que Sir Lord Baltimore domina «todos los trucos del heavy metal».

podcast.title: End of Collaboration with The Rolling Stones (1967)
podcast.body: Andrew Loog Oldham, who had been an instrumental producer in establishing The Rolling Stones' importance, officially ceased his collaboration with the band in late 1967. This decision was a rapid response to the commercial and critical setbacks the band experienced earlier that year. "se acabó oficialmente la etapa con André Olman, que fue el productor que los hizo tan importantes."

podcast.title: Uncomfortable Period for The Rolling Stones (1967-1968)
podcast.body: The Rolling Stones experienced a phase where they felt uncomfortable engaging with psychedelic music. This genre, combined with attempts at being overly commercial, led them to lose their essence, a situation from which they recovered with the success of "Jumpin' Jack Flash." "estaban un poco arregufo entre una psicodelia entre la que no se movían cómodos y un intento por ser comerciales que no lo había hecho perder su esencia."

podcast.title: Collaboration with The Rolling Stones (1968-1973)
podcast.body: Jimmy Miller began his collaboration with The Rolling Stones in 1968, marking the start of a new, highly productive era for the band. His work as a producer with the band continued until 1973, a period recognized as The Rolling Stones' "golden age." "empieza una nueva etapa que sería la etapa durada de los Rolling Stones hasta precisamente en 1973 cuando Jimmy Miller acaba su trabajo de colaboración con los Rolling Stones."

podcast.title: "Good Vibrations" as Psychedelic
podcast.body: The Beach Boys' "Good Vibrations" was described as "psychedelic and hip-hop in equal parts," highlighting its innovative and experimental sound for the mid-1960s. "canción psicodelica y hip hop a partes iguales."

srcs.episode: El Álbum Perdido que pudo cambiar la música ｜ Smile de The Beach Boys

podcast.title: Baroque and Complex Evolution
podcast.body: Psychedelia, alongside progressive rock, contributed to rock music becoming baroque, complex, elaborate, and at times pretentious, departing from its original youthful and rebellious spirit. "la música roque gracias al roque progresivo y a la psicodelia se convertió en música muy barroca, muy compleja, muy trabajada, muy recargada, a veces incluso un tanto pretenciosa."

srcs.episode: Qué es el NO WAVE. Es mucho más que música

podcast.title: Element in Bomberman Hero Soundtrack
podcast.body: The soundtrack for Bomberman Hero, while primarily focused on drum and bass, ventured into other musical territories, including psychedelia. This demonstrated composer Jun Chikuma's imaginative approach to scoring video games. "no temes saltar otros territorios, psicodelia, jazz, incluso pasajes cercanos al launch."

srcs.episode: Por qué los videjuegos de los 2000 sonaban así? Jungle⧸Drum and Bass

podcast.title: Golden Age Inaugurated by Pet Sounds
podcast.body: While *Pet Sounds* by The Beach Boys may not have directly inaugurated the genre of psychedelia, it is credited with inaugurating its "golden age." This highlights its profound impact on the development and popularization of psychedelic music and aesthetics. "el Pet Sounds inauguraba, posiblemente no inauguraba la psicodelia, pero sí inauguraba la época dorada de la psicodelia."

podcast.title: Influence on Dreampop and Shoegaze
podcast.body: The drone effect, first identified in The Velvet Underground's music, is noted as a technique that later appeared in psychedelic music, as well as shoegaze and dreampop, indicating a shared sonic lineage.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: MGMT's Sound Element
podcast.body: Psychedelia was described as an element sprinkled into MGMT's indie pop sound, contributing to their experimental and diverse musical approach in the early 2000s. "They had an indie pop sound sprinkled with various bits of psychedelia."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Modern "New Wave" Application
podcast.body: The term "New Wave" has been re-applied in later periods to describe new waves of music, specifically referencing the new wave of modern psychedelia, exemplified by artists like Tame Impala. "la expresión New Wave se ha usado mucho para hacer referencia a la nueva oleada del Asico de Lea Moderna, pues por ejemplo de Tamín Pala y de toda esta gente."

podcast.title: Modern Psychedelic Material
podcast.body: Dreampop is described as overlapping with anything resembling modern psychedelic material, showcasing a connection between the genres.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Musical Exploration
podcast.body: Psychedelia is noted as an element integrated into contemporary music, contributing to its diverse soundscapes. "incluso de la psicodelia."

podcast.title: Popularity of Pitch Shifting/Speed Variations
podcast.body: The technique of recording at different speeds and interspersing these variations during playback, which generates complex musical textures and interesting sound effects, became quite popular within the psychedelic genre, especially after its prominent use in *Sgt. Pepper's*. "sobre todo en la psicodelia la verdad es que se hizo bastante popular."

podcast.title: Reaction Against Psychedelia's Philosophy
podcast.body: The philosophy of psychedelic music and rock was a significant catalyst for the punk movement, which emerged as an important reaction against its perceived over-elaboration and complexity. "el pack tiene un importantísimo componente de reacción a esa filosofía de lo que era la música psicodélica y el roxico delico."

podcast.title: Tasked with Restoring American Essence
podcast.body: Jimmy Miller was specifically sought out by Mick Jagger to help The Rolling Stones reclaim their "American essence" in their music. This cultural and sonic influence was perceived as vital for their continued importance and success. "Necesitaba un productor que les yese, otra vez, esa esencia americana que tan importantes los había hecho. Entonces, considen contactar con Jimmy Miller."
